title: Machine fuzz
summary: Bass through a guitar rig, doing the whole guitar section's job. Garage and dance-punk, where the riff is the bass.
notes: Early Death From Above 1979 — a bass doing the job of the whole guitar section, so it is a bass through a guitar rig rather than a bass with a distortion knob, and it is the first voice to use the amp outside pluck/lead. Four things make it that record instead of a fuzz pedal. The drive is fed the low strings on purpose: `tighten` sits at 42 Hz, not the guitars' 150–260, because the intermodulation of a fundamental against its own harmonics is what makes one bass sound like a bass and a guitar at once — the mud the brown rig engineers out is the entire point here. The honk is at 1600 Hz, an octave below the HM-2 band the guitar voices bump, and the cab shuts at 3.2 kHz: fuzz bass is woolly and midrange-forward, and anything above that reads as a fizzy guitar rather than a big bass. Sag is light (3:1 at -18 dB) because this is dance-punk before it is doom — the eighth notes have to arrive as separate hits, and a hard ratio turns a driving riff into one sustained chord. And it is narrow (0.14) and short: 0.35 s release, decay-dominant to a 0.7 sustain, so a riff at 150 BPM stays a riff. The oscillator is a fat square at 14 cents — square because fuzz is a squaring curve and starting from odd harmonics beats manufacturing them, narrow because detune that reads as thickness on a guitar chord reads as a tuning problem down at E1.
